meta.name: ChefFlow pattern registry
meta.definition: A pattern is a complete assembly built from registered components. It is not page-specific code copied around. If you find yourself rebuilding one of these, you are duplicating a pattern.
meta.rule: Declare the surface mode before you lay anything out (docs/specs/surface-grammar-governance.md). Then pick the pattern. Then compose it from the component registry.

surfaceModes.rule: Every authenticated shell stamps data-cf-portal and data-cf-surface on its root element. The mode sets the shell budget and the allowed primitives. Declaring it is mandatory before layout.

shells.purpose: The one place fonts, providers, metadata and viewport are configured.
provides: AppThemeProvider (next-themes, class attribute, light default, system disabled)
rules: Never load a font anywhere else, with the single scoped exception of the culinary board.
Never add a redirect gate here.
themeColor and manifest live here, nowhere else.

shells.background: --page-bg-gradient plus three fixed radial ambient glows

shells.purpose: The operator product. The largest shell in the app.
anatomy: ChefMainContent (max-w-content mx-auto px-4 py-6 sm:px-6 lg:px-8)
rules: Never add a full-page onboarding blocker or redirect gate here. Onboarding is opt-in and the dashboard banner is the only nudge.
Heavy chrome is always nextDynamic ssr:false, never a static import.

shells.purpose: Platform admin. Uses its own admin-shell nav components.
Top-nav, no sidebar. main is mx-auto max-w-7xl px-4 py-6 sm:px-6 lg:px-8.
Chromeless outreach landings. Zero ChefFlow branding, deliberately.
Full-screen touch. select-none, noindex, userScalable false.
shells.note: userScalable:false fails WCAG 1.4.4. Justified only because it is a dedicated fixed-hardware kiosk; never copy it to a normal route.

shells.purpose: @page margins, .no-print hidden. Print is a real output surface with its own rules.
A sibling *-hub-nav.tsx above {children}. This is how you add tabbed sub-sections without duplicating chrome.
Sticky md:w-60 sidebar plus SettingsSearch, content capped at max-w-3xl px-4 py-6.
rules: Settings content never stretches to the full viewport. Cap at 680-800px.
Row height 44-56px. Card padding 16-24px. 24-32px between groups, 8-12px between rows.
Cards group 3-8 related settings. Never one card per toggle.

sections: Hero with layered radial background and HeroBackgroundImage
rules: Exactly one primary CTA above the fold.
Text over the hero photograph uses .media-scrim, never a flat colour wash.
The sticky mobile CTA is driven by an IntersectionObserver on #hero-cta-sentinel, not by a scroll listener.

anatomy: one primary CTA plus at most one secondary
rules: Background media must never reduce heading contrast below 4.5:1.
Ken Burns and parallax are suppressed under reduced motion.

anatomy: 2 to 4 feature cards or an icon grid
patterns.contentLimits: Never more than 7 items in one group.

rules: The image is the message. Do not bury it under an aggressive gradient.
Aspect ratio is fixed by the container so nothing shifts on load.
Every image has real alt text or is explicitly decorative.
Numbers shown must be computed from a real source. A figure not computed from a source is a rumour.
Never hide pricing.
No locked buttons and no Pro badges on disabled controls. The free path always executes; the upgrade prompt comes after the free action completes.

includes: ContactPage JSON-LD with ContactPoint and OpeningHoursSpecification

rules: Single column on mobile. Side-by-side fields cause input errors on a phone.
Inline validation as the user types, never only on submit.
Show step N of M. Autofill must work.
A sticky bottom CTA keeps the primary action in thumb reach.
Post-login restore goes through lib/session/recovery.ts getLastActivePath.
The UI is never the security boundary; the server gate must exist independently.

anatomy: zone sections, each in Suspense with a matching skeleton and a WidgetErrorBoundary
patterns.contentLimits: 2 hero metrics, 3-5 supporting, everything else in the detail tier.
rules: Adding a widget requires removing or consolidating something of equal or lesser value.
Vanity metric test: what decision would be made differently because of this number?

anatomy: page header with title and actions
rules: All five data states are handled: empty, loading, loaded, error, partial.
Never render a failed load as an empty list.
Use the shared hooks. There are already 12 domain filter bars; do not add a thirteenth bespoke one.
Debounce input through lib/hooks/use-debounce.ts.
Filter state belongs in the URL so a filtered view is shareable.
Hand-rolled, no cmdk. Mounted ssr:false from the chef shell.

patterns.rules: See the settings-shell entry above for the metrics.

rules: An empty state names the next action, it does not just say there is nothing here.

anatomy: otherwise a Card with a copyable error id, Try Again (reset), a portal home link and ErrorReportButton
rules: Every route group has an error.tsx. app/global-error.tsx is self-contained with inline styles because no provider is available at that point.
The skeleton mirrors the loaded layout so nothing jumps.
Use ListPageSkeleton / DetailPageSkeleton / FormPageSkeleton / GridPageSkeleton rather than a bespoke one.
Every portal has a mobile nav. Touch, open and close must work without hover.
Primary action reachable by thumb.
Safe-area insets via .pb-safe / .pt-safe / .pt-mobile-header.

patterns.purpose: Every authenticated portal renders a Suspense-wrapped rail strip. Follow the standard config rather than inventing a per-portal rail.
The repo's core composition idiom: a page-level _sections/ directory, a co-located section-skeletons.tsx, and every section wrapped in Suspense plus WidgetErrorBoundary.
patterns.rule: Any new dashboard-like page follows this triad. It is what keeps one slow or failing query from blanking a page.

rules: Print is a first-class output. Standard paper, thermal 80mm (48 columns) and thermal 58mm (32 columns) are all supported in globals.css.
!important is legitimate in a print block; it is not legitimate anywhere else.
Every share image is exactly 1200x630.
Satori needs inline styles; that is the one sanctioned place for them.
Twitter card is summary_large_image.
patterns.knownConflict: The OG routes say 'Ops for Artists' while layout.tsx and manifest.json say 'Food and Chef Marketplace'. See OPEN-CONFLICTS.md C-01.

patterns.purpose: The rendered visual catalog. The in-app route renders the real React primitives and is gated to the founder by app/(dev)/layout.tsx; the static copy is dependency-free, is built by npm run gallery:build and is verified in a real browser by npm run gallery:validate.
rules: The catalog is generated, never hand-maintained. If a component changes, rebuild rather than editing the catalog.
Any new component or variant appears here in the same change that adds it.
